title: Masked ICE Operation on Seattle Jet Bridge Sparks Chaos and Political Backlash
snippet: A targeted immigration arrest aboard an Alaska Airlines flight at Sea-Tac Airport left holiday travelers shaken, delayed a flight to Los Angeles, and drew fierce criticism from Washington officials.
content:
SEATTLE — A targeted enforcement operation by federal immigration agents at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport turned a routine holiday flight into a scene of panic Saturday morning, drawing sharp condemnation from airline representatives and state leaders.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers, dressed in plainclothes jackets and face coverings, boarded the jet bridge of Alaska Airlines Flight 1306 bound for Los Angeles to apprehend Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, a Mexican citizen whom federal authorities say overstayed his visa. However, the execution of the arrest during passenger boarding quickly escalated into a dramatic physical confrontation in front of stunned travelers.

Tension and Arrests During Boarding

Bystander video captured plainclothes officers struggling with a person on the floor of the crowded jet bridge as passengers carrying luggage looked on. In the footage, a woman can be heard screaming that her daughter was being taken and insisting she held a valid work authorization permit.

According to an ICE spokesperson, the situation escalated further when another traveler, identified as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, allegedly threw hot coffee at the officers during the arrest. Federal officials determined Hernandez Mejia was also in the country unlawfully after overstaying a visa. She was taken into custody and faces potential federal charges for assaulting an officer.

Airline and Airport Authorities Respond

Alaska Airlines expressed frustration over the timing and execution of the operation, noting that ICE officers provided no prior notification during one of the busiest travel weekends of the year. The airline confirmed the flight was delayed as a result.

"We recognize how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests," Alaska Airlines said in a statement, emphasizing its commitment to dignity and respect for all passengers. The carrier added that it is working alongside the Port of Seattle to examine whether standard protocols were followed and has raised concerns with federal officials.

The Port of Seattle, which manages Sea-Tac Airport, echoed those concerns, stating that local leaders plan to confer with federal authorities to better understand how the incident occurred inside a secure area.

Fierce Political and Union Backlash

The violent scene ignited immediate outrage from state leaders. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, denounced the tactics used by federal agents during a press conference alongside labor leaders, labeling the operation "deeply un-American."

"The video is horrific and it is chilling," Ferguson said, advocating for systemic overhaul. "We need a system of immigration enforcement and border security that is effective, ethical and humane. And ICE is not it."

Ferguson added that state authorities are reviewing how agents gained access to the jet bridge and whether their use of face coverings violated a state statute enacted in March that restricts law enforcement officers from hiding their faces during duty.

Labor organizations also criticized the disturbance. April Sims, president of the Washington State Labor Council, AFL-CIO, highlighted that union members were aboard the plane when the chaos unfolded. "Airport workers are already managing extraordinary stress, passengers are already anxious and instead of restoring calm and confidence, federal agents introduced more fear and more chaos," Sims said.

The incident reflects a broader surge in ICE enforcement at major U.S. transportation hubs over recent months, with federal agents increasingly focusing on individuals who remain in the country past their visa expiration dates.
